BINTSHATI:v1p154/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p154/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v1p154/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes remembering as recalling after forgetting and compares the Day when God reports people's deeds, which they had forgotten.
BINTSHATI:v1p154/r4.anchor: يوم يبعثهم الله جميعاً فينبئهم بما عملوا أحصاه الله ونسوه

NAHHAS:v4p374/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p374/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p374/r1.claim: يوم is governed by عذاب; Basran grammarians reject building it when followed by a future verb, reserving that for a following past or indeclinable form.
NAHHAS:v4p374/r1.anchor: العامل في يوم عذاب ولا يجوز عند البصريين أن يكون مبنيا إذا كان بعده فعل مستقبل

NAHHAS:v4p374/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p374/r2.speaker: الكوفيون
NAHHAS:v4p374/r2.claim: The Kufans say يوم is built because it has the sense of إذا.
NAHHAS:v4p374/r2.anchor: فأما الكوفيون فيقولون إنما بني لأنه بمعنى إذا فيبنى لبنائها

NAHHAS:v4p374/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p374/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p374/r3.claim: جميعا is a circumstantial accusative: God raises them from their graves to the Resurrection all together.
NAHHAS:v4p374/r3.anchor: ( جميعا ) منصوب على الحال أي يوم يبعثهم الله

NAHHAS:v4p374/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p374/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p374/r4.claim: God informs them of what they did, including what they concealed and other deeds.
NAHHAS:v4p374/r4.anchor: أي فيخبرهم بما أسروه وأخفوه وغير ذينك من أعمالهم

NAHHAS:v4p374/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p374/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p374/r5.claim: God counted, recorded, and preserved the deeds that their actors forgot.
NAHHAS:v4p374/r5.anchor: أي عده وأثبته وحفظه ونسيه عاملوه

NAHHAS:v4p374/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p374/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p374/r6.claim: God witnesses and knows every one of their deeds.
NAHHAS:v4p374/r6.anchor: أي على كل شيء من أعمالهم شاهد عالم به

SAMIN-DURR:58:6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:58:6/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:58:6/r1.claim: يوم may be accusative as the time of عذاب مهين.
SAMIN-DURR:58:6/r1.anchor: أحدها: أنه منصوب ب " عذاب مهين ". الثاني: أنه منصوب بفعل مقدر

SAMIN-DURR:58:6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:58:6/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:58:6/r2.claim: Abu al-Baqa supplies a passive verb such as they are humiliated or punished, or says their state is established on that day.
SAMIN-DURR:58:6/r2.anchor: فقدره أبو البقاء " يهانون أو يعذبون " ، أو استقر لهم ذلك يوم يبعثهم

SAMIN-DURR:58:6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:58:6/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:58:6/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari estimates اذكر for يوم, as a way to magnify the day; he also connects it to لهم through the predicate's implied state.
SAMIN-DURR:58:6/r3.anchor: وقدره الزمخشري ب اذكر قال: " تعظيما لليوم ". الثالث: أنه منصوب ب " لهم "

SAMIN-DURR:58:6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:58:6/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:58:6/r4.claim: Abu al-Baqa attaches يوم to أحصاه, but al-Samin finds this awkward because its pronoun refers to what they did.
SAMIN-DURR:58:6/r4.anchor: أنه منصوب ب " أحصاه " قاله أبو البقاء. وفيه قلق؛ لأن الضمير في " أحصاه " يعود

ZAJJAJ:v5p136#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p136#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p136#2/r1.claim: The accusative yaum connects to the preceding “humiliating punishment”: God raises them all together at one time.
ZAJJAJ:v5p136#2/r1.anchor: (يوم) منصوب بمعنى قوله: وللكافرين عذاب مهين

ZAJJAJ:v5p136#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p136#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p136#2/r2.claim: God informs them of their deeds so they recognize the proof binding against them.
ZAJJAJ:v5p136#2/r2.anchor: فينبئهم بما عملوا). أي يخبرهم بذلك ليعلموا وجوب الحجة عليهم.

ASAD-NOTES:58:intro/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:58:intro/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:58:intro/r3.claim: The surah moves through faith and its absence and their social effects, hypocrisy, and believers' proper attitude toward non-believers.
ASAD-NOTES:58:intro/r3.anchor: questions of faith and its absence

ASAD-NOTES:58:5/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:58:5/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:58:5/r2.claim: On resurrection, God will disclose all their deeds, which He recorded though they forgot, for He witnesses everything.
ASAD-NOTES:58:5/r2.anchor: God will have taken [all of ] it into account

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p209/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p209/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p209/r2.claim: The sūra checks clandestine anti-Islamic propaganda, reprimands the hypocrites, and directs Muslims to take measures; it also models sincerely bringing a difficulty to the Prophet and trusting God to resolve it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p209/r2.anchor: the hypocrites are severely reprimanded for indulging in such subversive activities, and in order to curb them, Muslims are also directed to adopt certain measures.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p209/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p209/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p209/r4.claim: Those who use real or hypothetical difficulty as a pretext for anti-Islamic propaganda open a war front against God and His Messenger, face humiliation, and cannot prevail over God's and the prophets' cause.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p209/r4.anchor: It is the incontestable decision of God that success and dominance is only reserved for God and His prophets.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p209/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p209/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p209/r5.claim: The hypocrites whisper evil suggestions to others and malign Islam's cause.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p209/r5.anchor: busy whispering evil suggestions to others and maligning the cause of Islam.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p210/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p210/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p210/r1.claim: The hypocrites disrespected the Prophet and treated God's forbearance in not punishing them as proof of their own correctness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p210/r1.anchor: by not punishing them as a proof of their correct attitude.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p210/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p210/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p210/r2.claim: They are warned of humiliation in this world, as history shows, and grievous punishment in the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p210/r2.anchor: they shall not only be humiliated in this world as history testifies, but will also face a grievous torment in the Hereafter.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p216/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p216/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p216/r9.claim: The people in view appeared to belong to the Muslims but were nurtured by Jews and operated among Muslims as their agents.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p216/r9.anchor: Though these people were apparently included among the Muslims, they were nurtured and supported by the Jews, and were working among the Muslims as their agents.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p216/r11.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p216/r11.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p216/r11.claim: Their whispered schemes are exposed: God knows every whisper and they will soon face its consequences.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p216/r11.anchor: the Almighty is aware of each and every whisper of theirs and soon they will face its consequences.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p219/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p219/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p219/r5.claim: The accusative yawm could attach to the previous verse’s punishment, but he prefers an omitted verb under standard Arabic principles.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p219/r5.anchor: however, in my opinion, it is because of a suppressed verb as per common linguistic principles of Arabic

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p219/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p219/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p219/r6.claim: Their worldly punishment is only a prelude; they must remember the day God resurrects them and brings their actions before them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p219/r6.anchor: they should also remember the day when the Almighty will raise them to life again

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p219/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p219/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p219/r7.claim: Jamiʿan indicates that all elements and motives of the conspiracies will be assembled and each person shown who proposed or followed what.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p219/r7.anchor: points to the fact that all the components and motives of the conspiracies

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p219/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p219/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p219/r8.claim: God’s informing them of their deeds entails their consequences, so they will face what they did.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p219/r8.anchor: The Almighty will inform them of all their deeds so that they face their consequences.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p219/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p219/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p219/r9.claim: Human forgetfulness does not mean God has forgotten: He recorded every deed and fixed a day for the reward and punishment of each person.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p219/r9.anchor: are meant to dispel a great misconception: people should not think that if they have forgotten everything they had done

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p219/r10.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p219/r10.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p219/r10.claim: The closing declaration that God witnesses all things substantiates the assurance that He has not forgotten their deeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p219/r10.anchor: substantiate what is just said: The Almighty is not

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p220/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p220/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p220/r1.claim: God is absent from nowhere; everything that happens in heaven and earth occurs before Him, and He is omnipresent.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p220/r1.anchor: whatever happens in the heavens and the earth happens before Him and He is omnipresent.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p130/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p130/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p130/r5.claim: They will swear to God in the resurrection just as they swear to believers, claiming they were not polytheists; their habitual worldly lying continues in the Hereafter, and they imagine their falsehood benefits them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p130/r5.anchor: فيحلفون له: أي لله تعالى. ألا ترى إلى قولهم: والله ربنا ما كنا مشركين ؟ كما يحلفون لكم أنهم مؤمنون، وليسوا بمؤمنين

ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r1.claim: يوم may be governed by the constituent attached to the preceding lām or by مهيمن.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r1.anchor: منصوب بما تعلق به اللام من الأستقرار أو بمهيمن

ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, an omitted remember governs يوم, magnifying and making the Day awe-inspiring.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r2.anchor: بإضمار اذكر أي اذكر ذلك اليوم تعظيما له وتهويلا

ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r3.claim: Another parse supplies an omitted يكون as an answer to when their punishment is: it will be on the Day He raises them.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r3.anchor: جواب لمنسألأ متى عذاب هؤلاء فقيل له

ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r4.claim: Making يوم governed by الكافرين is judged baseless.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r5.claim: جميعا may emphasize that not one of them will escape resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r5.anchor: حال جيء به للتأكيد والمعنى يبعثهم الله تعالى كلهم

ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r6.claim: Alternatively, جميعا means they will be gathered together on one plain.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون حالا غير مؤكدة أي يبعثهم مجتمعين في صعيد واحد

ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r7.claim: God will inform them of their vile deeds by explaining that the deeds issued from them.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r7.anchor: ببيان صدورها عنهم أو بتصويرها في تلك النشأة

ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r8.claim: Alternatively, their deeds appear in forms suited to that realm, terrifying them before witnesses and increasing their shame and punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r8.anchor: الصور الهائلة على رءوس الأشهاد تخجيلا لهم وتشهيرا بحالهم

ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r9.claim: The sentence answers how God can report passing deeds: He counted them exhaustively, and none escaped His count.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r9.anchor: استئناف وقع جوابا عما نشأ مما قبله من السؤال

ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r10.claim: ونسوه can be a circumstantial clause describing the deeds when God counted them, with or without an implicit قد.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r10.anchor: حال منمفعول أحصى بإضمار قد أو بدونه

ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r11.claim: Alternatively, they forgot their deeds, so God will disclose them and show that the punishment they witness came from those deeds, deepening reproach and regret.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r11.anchor: أحصاه الله تعالى ونسوهفينبئهم به ليعرفوا

ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r12.claim: Nothing at all is absent from God’s witness; this parenthetical conclusion confirms His exhaustive recording of their deeds.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r12.anchor: لا يغيب عنه أمر من الأمور أصلا والجملة اعتراض تذييلي

ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p22#2/r13.claim: The following verse is cited as evidence that God’s witness encompasses all things in the heavens and earth, whether contained in or constitutive of them.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p54#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p54#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p54#2/r3.claim: On the day God raises everyone and reports their deeds, He has preserved and counted those deeds even though they forgot them; He witnesses everything.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p54#2/r3.anchor: يوم يبعثهم الله جميعا فينبئهم بما عملوا أحصاه الله} حفظ الله أعمالهم {ونسوه والله على كل شيء شهيد

BAYDAWI-FULL:58:6-7/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:58:6-7/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:58:6-7/r1.claim: يوم is accusative through مهين or an implied اذكر.
BAYDAWI-FULL:58:6-7/r1.anchor: منصوب ب { مهين } أو بإضمار اذكر

BAYDAWI-FULL:58:6-7/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:58:6-7/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:58:6-7/r2.claim: All means none is left unresurrected, or that they are gathered together.
BAYDAWI-FULL:58:6-7/r2.anchor: كلهم لا يدع أحدا غير مبعوث

BAYDAWI-FULL:58:6-7/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:58:6-7/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:58:6-7/r3.claim: God informs them publicly before all witnesses, exposing their state and establishing punishment.

BAYDAWI-FULL:58:6-7/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:58:6-7/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:58:6-7/r4.claim: God counted everything without omission; they forgot through its abundance or their collusion in it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:58:6-7/r4.anchor: أحاط به عددا لم يغب منه شيء

BAYDAWI-FULL:58:6-7/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:58:6-7/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:58:6-7/r5.claim: Nothing is absent from God's witnessing.
BAYDAWI-FULL:58:6-7/r5.anchor: والله على كل شيء شهيد } لا يغيب عنه شيء

BIQAI-FULL:v7p474#s058/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p474#s058/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p474#s058/r1.claim: Al-Mujadilah warns that God will inflict severe punishment on those who oppose him and his Messenger; complete knowledge entails complete power and encompasses every perfection.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p474#s058/r1.anchor: بمن حاد الله ورسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما له سبحانه من تمام العلم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p474#s058/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p474#s058/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p474#s058/r2.claim: The title refers to the opening story and the surah’s ending; the repeated comprehensive divine name throughout the story and every verse is unusually pervasive.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p474#s058/r2.anchor: وعلى ذلك دلت تسميتها بالمجادلة بأول قصتها وآخرها

BIQAI-FULL:v7p474#s058/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p474#s058/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p474#s058/r3.claim: Repeated divine names present believers who have erred or disobeyed under both majesty and perfection, showing that both descriptions apply to them.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p474#s058/r3.anchor: للدلالة على أن الأكثر منها المراد فيها بالخطاب من يصح أن ينظر إليه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p474#s058/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p474#s058/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p474#s058/r4.claim: The surah strongly condemns certain acts when believers commit them and does not legalize them to satisfy natural desire; the author contrasts them with eating and intercourse permitted on Ramadan nights.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p474#s058/r4.anchor: شدد النكير فيها حين وقع بعض أهل الإيمان

BIQAI-FULL:v7p474#s058/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p474#s058/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p474#s058/r5.claim: This reading supports the author’s earlier account of why al-Waqiʿah, al-Rahman, and al-Qamar lack the comprehensive divine name repeated in al-Mujadilah.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p474#s058/r5.anchor: وهذا مؤيد لما تقدم من سر إخلاء الواقعة والرحمن والقمر من هذا الاسم الجامع

BIQAI-FULL:v7p474#s058/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p474#s058/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p474#s058/r6.claim: In the basmala, Allah’s encompassing knowledge completes his power and attributes; al-Rahman gives generously by creating all and sending guides, while al-Rahim singles out his chosen with the favor of divine approval.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p474#s058/r6.anchor: الذي أحاط علمه فتمت قدرته فكملت جميع صفاته

BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r1.claim: After mentioning God's limits, the commentary moves from the implied promise to their keepers and the threat to violators to detail punishment and reassure believers of victory.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r1.anchor: ولما ذكر حدوده , ولوح بالعطف على غير معطوف عليه إلى بشارة حافظها

BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r10.claim: The punishment comes when God restores the explicitly mentioned disbelievers and the implicitly included believers to life, all gathered together.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r10.anchor: في وقت إعادة الملك الأعظم للكافرين المصرح بهم والمؤمنين المشار إليه أحياء كما كانوا { جميعا }

BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r11.claim: God will inform them fully and exhaustively of their deeds, exposing them and establishing the proof against them.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r11.anchor: أي يخبرهم إخبارا عظيما مستقصى { بما عملوا } إخزاء لهم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r12.claim: God has encompassed every deed in number, quality, time, and place, while people forgot the immense total and forgot sins through heedlessness.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r12.anchor: أحاط به عددا كما وكيفا وزمانا ومكانا

BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r13.claim: Their disregard of forgotten sins is itself disregard and audacity toward God.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r13.anchor: ونسوا ما فيه المعاصي تهاونا بها , وذلك عين التهاون بالله والاجتراء عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r14.speaker: القشيري
BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r14.claim: Al-Qushayri says that recalling a sin during judgment brings such shame and regret that it eclipses every punishment; believers should obey, and if they slip, remember the sin and pray earnestly.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r14.anchor: قال القشيري : إذا حوسب أحد في القيامة على عمل عمله تصور له ما فعله

BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r15.claim: God is present, watchful, and preserving over absolutely everything; His encompassing, overpowering witness ensures perfect keeping.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r15.anchor: حفيظ حاضر لا يغيب , ورقيب لا يفعل

BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r16.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r16.claim: Abu Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr argues that the world glorifies God by its state and testifies to its dependence on a wise maker unlike His creation.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p486/r16.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : لما نزه سبحانه نفسه عن تقول الملحدين

BIQAI-FULL:v7p487/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p487/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p487/r1.claim: Continuing Ibn al-Zubayr's argument, the sequence moves from the universe's praise in 57:1 to God's address to believers in 57:7, a shift in address.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p487/r1.anchor: 77 ( { سبح لله ما في السماوات والأرض } ) 77

BIQAI-FULL:v7p487/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p487/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p487/r2.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr compares this shift with al-Baqara: after classifying people, the discourse invites all humanity to worship, then turns to the Prophet about the angels.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p487/r2.anchor: وكان ذلك ضرب من الالتفات , والواقع هنا منه أشبه بقوله سبحانه في سورة البقرة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p487/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p487/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p487/r3.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr traces a sequence from rebuking Arab polytheists through the warnings of al-Qamar and al-Rahman to the afterlife in al-Waqiʿa, then God's transcendence and believers' address in al-Hadid.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p487/r3.anchor: غالب آيها جار على ذلك ومجدد له أولها سورة ( ص ) كما نبه عليه في سورة القمر

BIQAI-FULL:v7p487/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p487/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p487/r4.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says that after accounts of past peoples, creation, the afterlife, duties, and recompense are completed, later discourse chiefly turns to believers' rulings and salvation.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p487/r4.anchor: فلما كمل ذلك صرف الكلام إلى ما يخص المؤمنين في أحكامهم وتعريفهم بما فيه من خلاصهم

DURR-FULL:v8p79/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p79/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p79/r2.claim: Mujāhid explains يُحادون as opposing or contending.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r1.claim: “The day” may modify an implied predicate of the unbelievers’ humiliating punishment, modify “humiliating,” or be an object of an implied “remember.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون { يوم } ظرفا متعلقا بالكون المقدر في خبر المبتدأ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r2.claim: Treating “the day” as an object of an implied “remember” is a familiar Qurʾānic construction; Ibn ʿĀshūr compares 2:30.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r2.anchor: وهذا كثير في أسماء الزمان التي وقعت في القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r3.claim: The plural pronouns refer to those who oppose God and His Messenger and the opponents mentioned before them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r3.anchor: وضمير الجمع عائد إلى الذين يحادون الله ورسوله } و { الذين من قبلهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r4.claim: “All together” is a circumstantial accusative describing the plural pronoun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r4.anchor: ولذلك أتى بلفظ الشمول وهو { جميعا } حالا من الضمير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r5.claim: Their being informed of their deeds threatens exposure of their hypocrisy at resurrection and serves as a euphemism for requital.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r5.anchor: وقوله : { فينبئهم بما عملوا } تهديد بفضح نفاقهم يوم البعث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r6.claim: “God recorded it and they forgot it” is a circumstantial clause attached to “what they did”; its point lies especially in their forgetting.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r6.anchor: وجملة { أحصاه الله ونسوه } في موضع الحال من ( ما عملوا )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r7.claim: God has known their deeds in full detail all along, while they forgot them in life, exposing their heedlessness and delusion; they will be astonished when confronted with the record.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r7.anchor: أي علمه الله علما مفصلا من الآن ، وهم نسوه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r8.claim: The scene recalls the criminals finding every small and great deed recorded and present in the Book, as described in al-Kahf 18:49.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r8.anchor: قال تعالى : { ووضع الكتاب فترى المجرمين مشفقين مما فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r9.claim: The closing statement is a summation; “witness” here means knowing the matters that are observed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p24/r9.anchor: وجملة { والله على كل شيء شهيد } تذييل . والشهيد : العالم بالأمور المشاهدة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p275#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p275#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p275#2/r1.claim: These verses through the end of the discussion of private talk were revealed about hypocrites and Jews in Medina who harassed believers, plotted against them, wished them harm, and whispered about it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p275#2/r1.anchor: هذه الآيات نزلت في منافقين وقوم من اليهود كانوا في المدينة يتمرسون برسول الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p275#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p275#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p275#2/r9.claim: The adverb yawm is governed by mahīn in the preceding verse, or can be governed by an implicit verb meaning remember.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p275#2/r9.anchor: العامل في: يوم قوله: مهين، ويحتمل أن يكون فعلا مضمرا تقديره: اذكر.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p275#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p275#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p275#2/r10.claim: Their forgetting is literal: an unbeliever does not retain the details of his deeds.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p275#2/r10.anchor: وقوله: ونسوه نسيان على بابه، لأن الكافر لا يحفظ تفاصيل أعماله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p275#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p275#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p275#2/r11.claim: After declaring Himself witness over everything, God directly warns Muhammad in a way shared by the whole Muslim community.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p275#2/r11.anchor: ولما أخبر تعالى أنه على كل شيء شهيد وقف محمد عليه السلام توقيفا تشاركه فيه أمته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p187#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p187#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p187#3/r1.claim: God will raise them from their graves and inform them of their sins and neglected duties; He preserved their deeds though they forgot them and witnesses all they do, openly or in secret.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p187#3/r1.anchor: أي من قبورهم فينبئهم بما عملوا من معاصيه وتضييع فرائضه أحصاه الله أي حفظه الله عليهم ونسوه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p41#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p41#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p41#2/r4.claim: On Resurrection, God gathers the first and last people together on one plain and tells them what good and evil they did.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p41#2/r4.anchor: وذلك يوم القيامة، يجمع الله الأولين والآخرين في صعيد واحد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p41#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p41#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p41#2/r5.claim: God has counted and preserved their deeds even though they have forgotten them; He witnesses everything, so nothing is absent, hidden, or forgotten from Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p41#2/r5.anchor: أي: ضبطه الله وحفظه عليهم، وهم قد نسوا ما كانوا عليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p41#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p41#2/r8.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p41#2/r8.claim: Ahmad observes that the passage opens with knowledge and closes with knowledge.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p41#2/r8.anchor: قال الإمام أحمد: افتتح الآية بالعلم، واختتمها بالعلم

BURSEVI:v9p324/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p324/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p324/r1.claim: The phrase “on the day” is governed by an omitted “remember,” magnifying and making the day of Judgment fearful.
BURSEVI:v9p324/r1.anchor: منصوب باذكر المقدر تعظيما لليوم وتهويلا له

BURSEVI:v9p324/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p324/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p324/r2.claim: The day is the Resurrection, when God revives the dead for recompense.
BURSEVI:v9p324/r2.anchor: والمراد يوم القيامة أي يحييهم الله بعد الموت للجزاء

BURSEVI:v9p324/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p324/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p324/r3.claim: “All together” either emphasizes the pronoun by excluding anyone from resurrection or describes them assembled at one time.
BURSEVI:v9p324/r3.anchor: أي كلهم بحيث لا يبقى منهم أحد غير مبعوث فيكون تأكيدا للضمير أو مجتمعين في حالة واحدة

BURSEVI:v9p324/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p324/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p324/r4.claim: God exposes their foul deeds by stating their source or showing them as terrifying forms suited to that realm, to shame them publicly and intensify punishment; mere information would serve no purpose.
BURSEVI:v9p324/r4.anchor: من القبائح ببيان صدورها منهم أو بتصويرها في تلك النشأة بما يليق بها من الصور الهائلة

BURSEVI:v9p324/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p324/r5.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v9p324/r5.claim: Al-Raghib defines iḥṣāʾ as exact enumeration, related to pebbles because people counted by fingers.
BURSEVI:v9p324/r5.anchor: الإحصاء التحصيل بالعدد يقال أحصيت كذا وذلك من لفظ الحصى

BURSEVI:v9p324/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p324/r6.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v9p324/r6.claim: Another gloss says iḥṣāʾ is counting with comprehensive control; it is more specific than ordinary counting, which does not entail completeness.
BURSEVI:v9p324/r6.anchor: الإحصاء عد بإحاطة وضبط إذ أصله العدد بآحاد الحصى للتقوى في الضبط فهو أخص من العد

BURSEVI:v9p324/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p324/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p324/r7.claim: They forgot their deeds because there were so many or because they committed them carelessly and did not believe they would matter.
BURSEVI:v9p324/r7.anchor: والحال أنهم قد نسوه لكثرته أو لتهاونهم حين ارتكبوه لعدم اعتقادهم

BURSEVI:v9p324/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p324/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p324/r8.claim: God’s being a witness means nothing is absent from Him; it requires recalling sins, weeping, and repenting before public exposure when excuses and pleas will not be accepted.
BURSEVI:v9p324/r8.anchor: فلا بد من استحضار الذنوب والبكاء عليها وطلب التوبة من الله الذي يحصى كل شيء ولا ينساه

BURSEVI:v9p324/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p324/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p324/r9.claim: God is present through knowledge, not bodily presence; therefore Qur’anic language that He is present gives no basis for declaring its speaker an unbeliever.
BURSEVI:v9p324/r9.anchor: واعلم أن القول بأنه تعالى شهيد قول بأنه حاضر لكن بالحضور العلمي لا بالحضور الجسماني فإنه منزه عن ذلك

MUQATIL:58:6/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:58:6/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:58:6/r1.claim: The verse concerns the hypocrites and their secret conversations, and the resurrection of all earlier and later people.
MUQATIL:58:6/r1.anchor: الأولين والآخرين نزلت في المنافقين في أمر المناجاة

MUQATIL:58:6/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:58:6/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:58:6/r2.claim: God preserved their evil deeds even though they themselves forgot them; he witnesses all their deeds.
MUQATIL:58:6/r2.anchor: يقول: حفظ الله أعمالهم الخبيثة، ونسوا هم أعمالهم { والله على كل شيء } من أعمالهم { شهيد }

NASAFI-FULL:v4p224#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p224#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p224#2/r1.claim: “The day” is accusative as governed by “humiliating,” or by an omitted “remember,” magnifying that day.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p224#2/r1.anchor: منصوب بمهين أو باضمارا ذكر تعظيما لليوم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p224#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p224#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p224#2/r2.claim: God resurrects all of them, leaving no one unraised, or brings them together in the same state.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p224#2/r2.anchor: كلهم لا يترك منهم أحد غير مبعوث أو مجتمعين في حال واحدة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p224#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p224#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p224#2/r3.claim: God informs them to shame, rebuke, and expose them publicly; overwhelmed with disgrace before witnesses, they wish to be rushed to Hell.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p224#2/r3.anchor: تخجيلا لهم وتوبيخا وتشهيرا بحالهم يتمنون عنده المسارعة بهم إلى النار

NASAFI-FULL:v4p224#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p224#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p224#2/r4.claim: God encompassed their deeds by counting them, missing nothing.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p224#2/r4.anchor: احاط به عددا لم يفته منه شيء

NASAFI-FULL:v4p224#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p224#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p224#2/r5.claim: They forgot their deeds because they were careless about them when committing them; people remember only matters they regard as important.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p224#2/r5.anchor: لانهم تهاونوا ونوابه حين ارتكبوه وانما تحفظ معظمات الامور

NASAFI-FULL:v4p224#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p224#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p224#2/r6.claim: God witnesses everything; nothing is absent from Him.

QURTUBI-FULL:58:5-6/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:58:5-6/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:58:5-6/r13.claim: Yawm is accusative either through attachment to humiliating punishment or an implied “remember,” which magnifies the Day.
QURTUBI-FULL:58:5-6/r13.anchor: نصب ب «عذاب مهين» أو بفعل مضمر تقديره واذكر تعظيما لليوم.

QURTUBI-FULL:58:5-6/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:58:5-6/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:58:5-6/r14.claim: God will resurrect men and women from their graves all at once.
QURTUBI-FULL:58:5-6/r14.anchor: أي الرجال والنساء يبعثهم من قبورهم في حالة واحدة

QURTUBI-FULL:58:5-6/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:58:5-6/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:58:5-6/r15.claim: God will tell them what they did in worldly life.
QURTUBI-FULL:58:5-6/r15.anchor: أي يخبرهم { بما عملوا } في الدنيا

QURTUBI-FULL:58:5-6/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:58:5-6/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:58:5-6/r16.claim: God recorded their deeds in books while they forgot them, so being shown the records makes the proof against them stronger.
QURTUBI-FULL:58:5-6/r16.anchor: عليهم في صحائف أعمالهم { ونسوه } هم حتى ذكرهم به في صحائفهم

QURTUBI-FULL:58:5-6/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:58:5-6/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:58:5-6/r17.claim: God is fully aware and observing; nothing is hidden from Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:58:5-6/r17.anchor: مطلع وناظر لا يخفى عليه شيء.

QASHANI:58:6-7/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:58:6-7/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:58:6-7/r1.claim: Their resurrection is their being raised from the resting places of their bodies.

QASHANI:58:6-7/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:58:6-7/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:58:6-7/r2.claim: Their deeds are disclosed because their forms have been imprinted on the tablets of their souls.
QASHANI:58:6-7/r2.anchor: لانتقاش صور أعمالهم في ألواح نفوسهم

QASHANI:58:6-7/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:58:6-7/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:58:6-7/r3.claim: God has enumerated the deeds by recording them in the four books mentioned.

QASHANI:58:6-7/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:58:6-7/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:58:6-7/r4.claim: They forgot their deeds because sensual pleasures and bodily preoccupations distracted and absorbed them.
QASHANI:58:6-7/r4.anchor: لذهولهم عنه باشتغالهم باللذات الحسية وانهماكهم في الشواغل البدنية

QASHANI:58:6-7/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:58:6-7/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:58:6-7/r5.claim: God is present with everything and watches over it.

RAZI-FULL:v29p228#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p228#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p228#2/r9.claim: The resurrection and accounting in the next verse complete the preceding threat of worldly abasement and punishment in the afterlife.
RAZI-FULL:v29p228#2/r9.anchor: ثم ذكر تعالى ما به يتكامل هذا الوعيد فقال

STUDYQURAN:58:intro/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:58:intro/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:58:intro/r10.claim: Verses 1–4 address ẓihār; verses 5–6 introduce opponents of God and His Messenger, the theme of the rest of the sūrah.
STUDYQURAN:58:intro/r10.anchor: vv. 5–6 introduce the discussion of those who oppose God and His Messenger

STUDYQURAN:58:6/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:58:6/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:58:6/r1.claim: The opening time phrase may modify the preceding humiliating punishment, or serve as the object of an implied verb meaning remember or mention.
STUDYQURAN:58:6/r1.anchor: The beginning of this verse is either a clause modifying humiliating punishment or the object of an implied verb

STUDYQURAN:58:6/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:58:6/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:58:6/r2.claim: On the implied-verb reading, the verse calls people to remember the gathering of every human on an open, barren plain for judgment.
STUDYQURAN:58:6/r2.anchor: make mention of the Day when God will

STUDYQURAN:58:6/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:58:6/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:58:6/r3.claim: God records people's deeds in a registry presented at Judgment; disbelievers then find every deed recorded, though they had forgotten.
STUDYQURAN:58:6/r3.anchor: God keeps account of people’s deeds in a book or registry that is then presented to them on the Day of Judgment

STUDYQURAN:58:6/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:58:6/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:58:6/r4.claim: The statement that God witnesses all things is linked to several verses; elsewhere the Quran says He witnesses what people do.
STUDYQURAN:58:6/r4.anchor: For God is Witness over all things, see also

QUSHAYRI:v3p296/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p296/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p296/r4.claim: At the Resurrection, a person's deeds are shown and recalled as though the person stood at the scene of the lapse, feeling shame and regret that eclipse every punishment.
QUSHAYRI:v3p296/r4.anchor: إذا حوسب أحد في القيامة على عمله تصور له ما فعله وتذكره ، حتى كأنه قائم في تلك الحاله عن بساط الزلة

QUSHAYRI:v3p296/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p296/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p296/r5.claim: A Muslim should avoid disobeying the Master; if a lapse occurs, keep it in mind and turn to God with earnest supplication.
QUSHAYRI:v3p296/r5.anchor: فسبيل المسلم ألا يحوم حول مخالفة أمر مولاه ، فإن جرى المقدور ووقع في هجنة التقصير فلتكن زلته على بال

TAB-FULL:v22p467#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p467#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p467#2/r1.claim: On the Resurrection, God summons them, discloses their deeds, and has counted and preserved what they forgot.
TAB-FULL:v22p467#2/r1.anchor: أحصى الله ما عملوا، فعده عليهم، وأثبته وحفظه، ونسيه عاملوه

TAB-FULL:v22p467#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p467#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p467#2/r2.claim: God counted, recorded, and preserved their deeds, while the people who did them forgot them.
TAB-FULL:v22p467#2/r2.anchor: أحصى الله ما عملوا، فعده عليهم، وأثبته وحفظه، ونسيه عاملوه

TAB-FULL:v22p467#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p467#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p467#2/r3.claim: God witnesses all they did and all else among His creation: He knows and encompasses it, and nothing escapes Him.
TAB-FULL:v22p467#2/r3.anchor: يقول: والله جل ثناؤه على كل شيء عملوه وغير ذلك من أمر خلقه {شهيد}

SULAMI:v2p314#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p314#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p314#2/r1.claim: One who forgets their offenses, does not weep or repent, and fails to seek forgiveness has wasted life; the deeds God counted will be displayed at the great assembly, when repentance and excuses no longer help.
SULAMI:v2p314#2/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : من نسي جرائمه ولم يكثر عليها بكاؤه ولم يتأسف عليها بالندم وطلب التوبة فقد ضيع عمره

TABATABAI:58:4-6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:58:4-6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:58:4-6/r3.claim: Muḥāddah means resistance and opposition; kabt means humiliation and disgrace.
TABATABAI:58:4-6/r3.anchor: المحادة الممانعة والمخالفة، والكبت الإذلال والإخزاء

TABATABAI:58:4-6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:58:4-6/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:58:4-6/r4.claim: Although verses 5–6 could begin a new discussion of opposition and its effects, the context makes them explain why the preceding verse forbids opposing God and the Messenger.
TABATABAI:58:4-6/r4.anchor: ظاهر السياق أن تكونا مسوقتين لتعليل ذيل الآية السابقة الذي معناه النهي

TABATABAI:58:4-6/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:58:4-6/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:58:4-6/r7.claim: The phrase on the day God raises them modifies the preceding promise of painful punishment for disbelievers.
TABATABAI:58:4-6/r7.anchor: في يوم يبعثهم الله وهو يوم الحساب والجزاء

TABATABAI:58:4-6/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:58:4-6/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:58:4-6/r8.claim: On the Day of Judgment God will inform them of the full reality of everything they did in worldly life.
TABATABAI:58:4-6/r8.anchor: وهو يوم الحساب والجزاء فيخبرهم بحقيقة جميع ما عملوا في الدنيا

TABATABAI:58:4-6/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:58:4-6/r9.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:58:4-6/r9.claim: Al-Rāghib defines iḥṣāʾ as securing a count; the term derives from pebbles used for counting, as fingers are used today.
TABATABAI:58:4-6/r9.anchor: قال الراغب الإحصاء التحصيل بالعدد يقال أحصيت كذا

TABATABAI:58:4-6/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:58:4-6/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:58:4-6/r10.claim: God’s witnessing everything explains how He has comprehensively enumerated their deeds.
TABATABAI:58:4-6/r10.anchor: تعليل بقوله { أحصاه الله } وقد مر تفسير شهادة الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p340/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p340/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p340/r1.claim: The preceding punishment will take place on the Day God raises them all.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p340/r1.anchor: ثم بين أن ذلك العذاب متى يكون فقال: {يوم يبعثهم الله جميعا}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p340/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p340/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p340/r2.claim: God preserved their deeds while they themselves forgot them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p340/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: حفظ الله أعمالهم ونسوا هم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:58:4-6/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:58:4-6/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:58:4-6/r9.claim: God will inform all the resurrected of their deeds so that they know the proof against them has been established.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:58:4-6/r9.anchor: يوم يبعثهم الله جميعا فينبئهم بما عملوا } يخبرهم بذلك ليعلموا وجوب الحجة عليهم { أحصاه الله } علمه الله وأحاط بعدده

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:58:4-6/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:58:4-6/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:58:4-6/r10.claim: God knew and encompassed the count of their deeds, while they themselves forgot them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:58:4-6/r10.anchor: أحصاه الله } علمه الله وأحاط بعدده { ونسوه } هم.

ELMALILI:58:5-6/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:58:5-6/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:58:5-6/r6.claim: God will resurrect them all together and disclose their deeds before witnesses, humiliating and disgracing them.
ELMALILI:58:5-6/r6.anchor: yaptıklarını kendilerine haber verecek şâhidler huzurunda

ELMALILI:58:5-6/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:58:5-6/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:58:5-6/r7.claim: Though people have forgotten their deeds, God has counted them one by one and entered them in their records.
ELMALILI:58:5-6/r7.anchor: Onlar onu unutmuşlarsa da Allah onu bir bir saymış, defterlerine geçirmiştir.

ELMALILI:58:5-6/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:58:5-6/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:58:5-6/r8.claim: God witnesses everything, and nothing escapes His knowledge.

BURHAN:v3p28/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p28/r1.speaker: القفال
BURHAN:v3p28/r1.claim: Al-Qaffal gives four aims of Israelite narratives: prove Muhammad’s prophethood through knowledge obtainable only by revelation; recount favors to Israel; explain their ancestors’ rejection of prophets and foreshadow descendants’ treatment of Muhammad; and warn contemporaries of punishment like that of their forebears.
BURHAN:v3p28/r1.anchor: وقال القفال 3 في تفسيره ذكر الله في أقاصيص بني اسرئيل

ITQAN:v4p539/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p539/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p539/r1.claim: The author presents the book as a synthesis of Qur'anic sciences and tafsirs, extracting their benefits and organizing material dispersed across many works.
ITQAN:v4p539/r1.anchor: وأخذت زبدها ودرها ومررت على رياض التفاسير على كثرة عددها واقتطفت ثمرها وزهرها

ITQAN:v4p539/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p539/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p539/r2.claim: He disclaims perfection, arguing that human beings are necessarily deficient and that he does not promise a work free of every flaw.
ITQAN:v4p539/r2.anchor: على أني لا أبيعه بشرط البراءة من كل عيب ولا أدعى أنه جمع سلامة كيف والبشر محل النقص بلا ريب

ITQAN:v4p539/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p539/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p539/r3.claim: He condemns ignorant, envious rivals who neglect religious law for philosophy, falsely malign scholars, and act as if no guardians record their words and deeds.
ITQAN:v4p539/r3.anchor: كأن الله لم يوكل بهم حافظين يضبطون أقوالهم وأعمالهم
